summary: The starter prompt is executable: it clearly defines a Node.js Mongoose daily batch processor that streams interest-bearing accounts and writes accrual journal documents with unordered bulk writes. Several implementation details (exact Node / Mongoose versions, model shapes, batch size, scheduling time, seed data, README / infra artefacts) are left to the builder's defaults or to follow-up. Installed skills provide useful guidance for driver best practices, indexing, data-model patterns, and connection tuning, so the build can start but will rely on assumptions for missing specifics.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "build a Node.js Mongoose batch processor ... queries all active interest-bearing account documents ... computes accrued interest ... writes each accrual as an immutable journal document using unordered bulk writes"
rubric.note: The business problem, user scenario, and what the sample demonstrates are explicit.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "batch processor that runs on a daily schedule" — a single scheduled process
rubric.note: This is a standalone scheduled app (no multi-agent orchestration required).

rubric.found_in_prompt: skill_md run environment: "Node.js 24 with npm and npx is available."
rubric.note: Node.js runtime (version 24) is provided in the run environment.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "Mongoose" (the ODM is specified) but no version
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use Mongoose 7.x (the current major compatible with Node 24) and the accompanying MongoDB driver 5.x; pin with caret ranges in package.json but include package-lock.json.
rubric.note: The documentdb-driver skill gives best-practice patterns (singleton client, reuse) but does not specify exact package versions.

rubric.found_in_prompt: skill_md: "A vector-capable Azure DocumentDB cluster (compute tier M30, MongoDB 7.0 wire protocol ...) is reachable ... connection string in env var DOCUMENTDB_URI"
rubric.note: The run environment explicitly identifies the live cluster and tier to use; the sample must use that cluster and database.

rubric.found_in_prompt: skill_md: "connection string is in the environment variable DOCUMENTDB_URI. Read it from the environment at run time. Never write its value into any file, log, README or test fixture; use a config file or .env.example with a placeholder"
rubric.note: Secrets location and handling (env var, do not commit) are stated in the run environment.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "account and journal documents defined as Mongoose models" (document types required) but shapes/fields not specified
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will define minimal models such as: Account {_id, balance: Number, interestRate: Number, status: 'active'|'closed', interestBearing: Boolean, updatedAt, schemaVersion}, Journal {_id, accountId: ObjectId, runDate: ISODate, amount: Number, createdAt: ISODate, immutable: true}. The journal is an insert-only reference to the account._id.
rubric.note: The prompt requires models but leaves exact fields / schemaVersion / immutability conventions to implementer; data-modeling skill provides guidance but not concrete shapes.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Include a seed script that creates a modest dataset (e.g., ~100 accounts with a mix of active/inactive and interest-bearing flags) and idempotently upserts by a unique account number so it can be re-run without duplication.
rubric.note: The starter prompt doesn't supply or require a seed dataset; none of the installed skills supply a concrete sample dataset for this banking example (documentdb-local-deployment helps manage local sample-data but not the specific seed content).

rubric.found_in_prompt: "queries all active interest-bearing account documents ... in cursor-paginated batches"
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Create an index to support the query, e.g., a partial/compound index on { status: 1, interestBearing: 1 } or a partial index with filter { status: 'active', interestBearing: true } to avoid COLLSCAN. Also create an index on journal.accountId for efficient lookups/aggregation if needed.
rubric.note: The prompt specifies the query pattern; documentdb-indexing gives index-selection guidance but the exact index definition (partial vs compound) must be chosen by the builder.
No embeddings or AI components are required by the prompt.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "runs on a daily schedule" — a scheduled batch processor
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Implement as a Node.js process with a small CLI and scheduler: an npm script (e.g., "start": "node ./dist/worker.js") and a built-in schedule via node-cron or a run-once CLI flag. Default cron schedule: "0 0 * * *" (midnight UTC) and provide a --once flag for manual runs.
rubric.note: The prompt specifies 'daily' but not the exact cron expression, timezone, or whether a hosted scheduler (Azure Functions / WebJob / CronJob) is desired.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Do not create new cloud resources; use the existing cluster available in the run environment. If infra-as-code is required later, the documentdb-azure-deployment skill can be used to provide Bicep/az CLI artifacts.
rubric.note: The starter prompt does not ask the builder to provision infrastructure. The skill exists but the prompt's run environment says an existing cluster should be used.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Include a README with commands: npm install, copy .env.example to .env and set DOCUMENTDB_URI, npm run seed, npm run start (or node --once). Provide a test command (npm test) where unit tests mock the DB so they run without a live cluster.
rubric.note: No explicit run/test commands are given in the prompt; the builder must author standard instructions.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Accept when: (1) scheduled job can be run manually with --once; (2) it iterates all active interest-bearing accounts using a cursor and batch size, (3) computes interest correctly for sample inputs, (4) writes a per-account insert-only journal entry for the run using Model.bulkWrite with ordered: false for each batch, and (5) the run has been verified against the live cluster per the run environment.
rubric.note: No explicit acceptance criteria provided; the builder will need to define concrete checks.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Keep costs low by not provisioning new clusters, follow TLS and env-var secret handling, and do not attempt production DR/CMK/HA configuration in the sample.
rubric.note: No cost/usage constraints or non-goals are given; the builder will pick sensible defaults.

rubric.found_in_prompt: skill_md: "Use the database named `sample_banking_20` ... connection string in env var DOCUMENTDB_URI. Never write its value ... use a config file or `.env.example` with a placeholder"
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Follow a conventional Node layout: src/, scripts/, tests/, package.json, package-lock.json, .env.example with placeholders for DOCUMENTDB_URI and other settings (BATCH_SIZE, RUN_ONCE flag), README.md explaining purpose and run steps.
rubric.note: Some conventions (DB name, DOCUMENTDB_URI) are given; others (folder layout, exact env var names beyond DOCUMENTDB_URI) are not fully specified.

contradictions: The prompt says "Using the DocumentDB skill" but there is no single installed skill named exactly "DocumentDB skill"; many specialized documentdb-* skills are installed instead. The builder will need to choose which skill(s) to consult.

Reference requirement item "Dependencies are pinned in requirements.txt" appears aimed at Python projects; the starter prompt requests a Node.js sample, so a requirements.txt artifact is not applicable.
questions_for_author: What exact daily schedule/time and timezone should the job use by default (e.g., midnight UTC: "0 0 * * *")?
Which Mongoose / mongodb driver versions should be targeted (or is using the latest Mongoose 7.x compatible with Node 24 acceptable)?
What batch size should the cursor pagination group into for bulkWrite operations (e.g., 500, 1000)?

Should journal insertions be idempotent across repeated runs (i.e., add a runId or dedupe key), or is simple insert-only sufficient? Should the journal document include run metadata (runId, host, timestamp)?
Do you want infrastructure-as-code (Bicep/Terraform/az CLI) included to provision the DocumentDB cluster, or should the sample explicitly avoid provisioning and rely on the provided cluster?
requirements_at_risk: .env.example lists every setting with placeholder values — not required by the starter prompt and not enforced by installed skills; builder may omit or incompletely declare env vars.
Vector index dimensions match the embedding model's output — not relevant to this sample (no embeddings are mentioned) and not covered by the prompt or skills for this use-case.
Vector index parameters chosen for the sample's data size and README instructions to change them — not covered; builder will likely omit vector index tuning.
Seed script loads sample data and creates the index, idempotent — the prompt doesn't mention providing a seed script; this is likely to be missed unless the builder adds one by assumption.
/search returns a clear error for an empty query and when the embedding call fails — the sample has no /search route; this requirement is at risk.
Search results include the similarity score — not applicable unless search/embeddings are added; at risk of being omitted.
Dependencies are pinned in requirements.txt — a Python-style requirement; Node projects use package.json/package-lock.json, so this requirement is at risk or inapplicable as stated.
Unit tests run without a live cluster — starter prompt doesn't require tests; absent further instruction, tests that mock the DB may not be provided.
Infrastructure for the cluster is provided as code, using the Azure DocumentDB resource type — prompt uses an existing cluster; infra-as-code is not requested and is likely to be missing.
README covers what the sample shows, prerequisites, setup, run, and clean-up — the prompt doesn't ask for a README explicitly; this may be omitted or incomplete.
